PASS: QA1 gate 1, round 1: PASS. Audited commit 79a5b47 against the current sprint file, re-read fresh. The file is unchanged since 1157755, and no criterion asserts anything between versions. Sprint 31 is merged and closed, so the dependency is met.

R1 Met. A grep of app/ and lib/ non-test source for "rite the horoscope", "Nothing has been written" and "not written yet" finds only:
- comments in app/date/[date]/actions.ts and lib/date-page/cast.ts;
- lib/llm/horoscope.ts:114, which is the OpenAI prompt text, not user-visible copy.
The idle sentence is R1's exact wording. The button reads "Reveal the horoscope", the pending label "Revealing…", and the busy phrase "The horoscope is being revealed." "Try again" is kept. The error and disabled messages are unchanged, as allowed.

R2 Met. Read both branches side by side.
- Unsaved: ReadingHeader("not revealed yet") + IdleBlock + readingFooter with button.castButton + note.
- Saved, folded: the same header classes and status text + the same IdleBlock + a summary holding span.readingFooter, span.castButton with the same label, and the same note text and class.
- The only structural difference is summary/span against button. Dev Team names it and it is unavoidable. .revealPanel is display:contents, so flex layout is unchanged.
- The test "folded, it can't be told apart..." asserts the shared pieces.
- The horoscope text lives only inside the details element, after the summary.

R3 Met.
- It is a native details/summary in HoroscopeReveal.tsx, which is not "use client" and has no state, effects or handlers.
- There is no fetch, and no new client component reveals the text. ReadingPanel was already the client component, for useFormStatus.
- The keyboard and expanded state come from the native element.
- The folded and open summary labels toggle with display:none, so only one is in the accessible name. The folded note is aria-hidden inside the summary.
- Paragraph rendering and the rise animation are the same as before.

R4 Met. Traced ?revealed=1.
- isLandingRevealed accepts exactly "1". The value only sets details open={revealed}, and both pages pass it through as a boolean.
- With no saved horoscope there is no details element, so it has no effect.
- Neither GET path gains a write. The only diff to either server action is the success redirect, now withRevealed(path). The error redirects are unchanged.
- reveal-landing.test.ts renders the REAL DatePage and ReadingPage. The admin client is mocked to throw if created, and the test asserts:
  - no from() or insert;
  - no set_reading_horoscope;
  - no openai.com fetch;
  - on the date page, only api.wikimedia.org fetches.
  It covers saved and unsaved horoscopes on both routes, plus the 0, true and repeated values.

R5 Met. DisabledReadingSection with a saved horoscope renders SavedHoroscope, with the disabled note as both folded note and footer, and no form or submit. With none, it renders the header, IdleBlock and disabled note, with no reveal control. The lookup-unavailable path still renders SavedHoroscopesUnavailable with no details element, and that is tested.

R6 and R7 Met. Nothing under supabase/, lib/ or DateNavigation* changes. The diff covers:
- the shared panel and view: ReadingPanel, ReadingView, the new HoroscopeReveal, reveal.ts and the CSS;
- both pages' wiring;
- both actions' success redirect, which R4 permits;
- tests;
- vitest.config.ts. That file gains an "@/" alias anchored to "^@/" so @supabase packages are untouched. It is test infrastructure only, and the commit says the user agreed to it; I have not verified that agreement myself.
The chart, events and navigation are not touched.

R8 Met. ReadingPanel.test.ts covers every listed state, asserting the visible text and that the text sits inside the folded details element:
- saved and folded;
- landing revealed;
- no horoscope with generation enabled;
- disabled, with and without a saved horoscope;
- error with Try again, with and without a saved horoscope.
reveal-landing.test.ts covers the lookup-unavailable state and the no-write GET.

Ran these myself:
- npm test: 27 files, 318 tests, green.
- typecheck: clean.
- lint: clean.
- build: clean, both routes dynamic.

Low, non-blocking, for LiveQA's eye:
(a) .reveal makes the details element a flex container. Older engines ignored display:flex on details and fell back to block, which loses the 20px gap but still unfolds. Check visually in LiveQA steps 1 and 6.
(b) In the saved-plus-error case, the error note shows beside the folded control, and "Try again" appears only once unfolded. That state needs a horoscope saved AND a failed cast, which only a racing double-cast can produce. It is tested and documented.

No Human Prerequisites. No test was labelled known-failing.
commit=deb75ad | ci=green: 1 CI run(s) for deb75ad91e423c8e296272889a88ede0a153334c all completed successfully with real steps executed.

CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL (round 1). There is one low-severity defect against R2, "the same look": on
desktop, the folded "Reveal the horoscope" control's label is LEFT-aligned when a horoscope
is saved, and CENTRED when none exists. Everything else passes.

Tested 2026-11-23, about 01:40 to 01:55 UTC, against https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app.
Shipped commit deb75ad. Production serves the pushed tip e461f27: /api/health/db reports
status ok and commit e461f27. git diff --stat deb75ad e461f27 touches only
docs/sprints/state/sprint-33.json, and 79a5b47..deb75ad likewise.
CI: runs 45094539804 (deb75ad) and 45095089748 (e461f27). build, rls-tests and migrate all
succeed in both.
Tools: headless Chromium (Playwright 1.57) with JS on and off, keyboard input, the CDP
accessibility tree, 1280x900 and 390x844 isMobile, plus curl against the anon RPC.

DEFECT (low, R2).
- Folded state on desktop (1280px):
  - /date/1969-07-20 (saved) and /reading/0b01c79f-... (saved): the label is the SUMMARY's
    span.castButton, 186x52px, text-align "start". "REVEAL THE / HOROSCOPE" sits flush left
    inside the box, after 18px padding.
  - /date/2031-05-09 (no horoscope): the label is BUTTON.castButton, 186x52px, text-align
    "center". The same two lines are centred, with the first line 53px from the box edge.
- Font (IBM Plex Mono 10.5px, 1.89px letter-spacing), colour, border, padding (11px 18px),
  size, idle sentence and badge "NOT REVEALED YET" are all identical between the two.
- Screenshots: s33-look-saved.png and s33-look-unsaved.png.
- At 390px both are 326x44 with text-align center, so there is no difference on the phone.
- Repro: open /date/1969-07-20 and any date with no horoscope side by side at desktop width,
  and compare the button label's alignment.
- Fix direction, not prescriptive: give the summary's castButton the same text-align (and
  justify) as the button.

PASSES.

STEP 1, saved date folded, reveal in page: PASS. /date/1969-07-20 with JS on:
- On load the chart svg and "What happened" are visible.
- The panel reads "The reading / NOT REVEALED YET / The chart stands as it is. Nothing has
  been revealed about it yet - reveal the horoscope when you want the sky held to account for
  the day." with the control "REVEAL THE HOROSCOPE".
- 0 of 3 horoscope paragraphs are visible, all inside a closed details element.
- Clicking the summary: the badge becomes "REVEALED", the summary "FOLD THE HOROSCOPE AWAY",
  and 3 of 3 paragraphs are visible ("Jupiter was in conjunction with Uranus on July 20,
  1969...").
- The URL is unchanged and there were zero requests during the reveal.
- The revealed text ends "Written on request from 10 positions and 17 aspects."
- With JS DISABLED (a separate context), the identical before and after: it opens natively,
  with no requests and the same URL.

STEP 2, date without a horoscope: PASS. LiveQA cast on 2030-03-14. That is a permanent
production reading, recorded so it isn't mistaken for organic use.
- Before: the identical copy and badge, the control a BUTTON "REVEAL THE HOROSCOPE".
- Clicked at 01:41:24Z. One POST to /date/2030-03-14. The pending state read "REVEALING /
  The horoscope is being revealed. / gpt-4o-mini - temperature 0.9" with the button
  "REVEALING..." disabled.
- The response redirected to /date/2030-03-14?revealed=1 (01:41:28Z). It landed REVEALED
  with "FOLD THE HOROSCOPE AWAY" open and text "On March 14, 2030, Mars sextile Pluto...".
- Reloading the plain /date/2030-03-14 opens folded ("NOT REVEALED YET", SUMMARY control).
  Revealing then made zero requests.

STEP 3, landing URL on a fresh date generates nothing: PASS as far as anon can observe.
- /date/2031-05-09?revealed=1, loaded twice: 200 each time, folded ("NOT REVEALED YET",
  "Reveal the horoscope" button), and zero non-GET requests, including 1.5s after load.
- rpc get_reading_by_date for 2031-05-09 returns [] both before and after.
- Also checked: /reading/5bf3a1f5-...?revealed=1 (an unwritten reading) is folded with no
  POST. /date/1969-07-20?revealed=1 opens revealed, with no POST.
- Not verified: the raw row count for 2031-05-09. Anon can only see rows with a horoscope,
  so a stray horoscope-less insert would be invisible to me. The user can confirm in the
  dashboard (readings where event_date = 2031-05-09 should be 0).

STEP 4, keyboard: PASS.
- On /date/1969-07-20, Tab reached the SUMMARY "REVEAL THE HOROSCOPE" after 20 presses.
- Enter opened it (3 paragraphs visible), Space closed it (0), Space opened it again (3).
- CDP accessibility tree for the summary: role DisclosureTriangle, name "REVEAL THE
  HOROSCOPE", expanded=false when folded; name "FOLD THE HOROSCOPE AWAY", expanded=true when
  open.

STEP 5, /reading/[id] with a horoscope: PASS. /reading/0b01c79f-73d5-4fbc-afeb-d65da32ae38d
behaves identically to step 1, with JS on and off: folded, the same copy, then reveal in
place with the same URL.
- With JS on, the reveal triggered two GET fetches of /date/1969-07-20?_rsc=... These are
  Next.js prefetches of the "Go to this date" link becoming visible inside the revealed
  content. They are not navigation and not a reveal request. With JS off there were zero.

STEP 6, 390px: PASS.
- /date/1969-07-20, /reading/0b01c79f-... and /date/2031-05-09: scrollWidth is 390, both
  folded and revealed.
- Revealed at 390px, chart svg, rect and circle elements extend past 390px but are clipped
  (scrollWidth stays 390). That is the chart's own existing overflow, with no horizontal
  scroll.

No console or page errors anywhere.

PASS: QA1 live-loop audit of fix commit 50af882 (LiveQA round 1 CONDITIONAL, R2 label alignment): PASS.

LiveQA's defect: on desktop, the folded saved-state control is span.castButton inside the summary, and it inherited text-align start. The unsaved state's button.castButton gets centre alignment from the UA stylesheet. Font, size, padding, border and colour were otherwise identical by LiveQA's measurement.

The fix: deb75ad..50af882 changes app/reading/[id]/reading.module.css only, besides the state file. It adds 8 lines: a commented rule, .revealSummary .castButton { text-align: center }.
- It is scoped to the summary's span. Specificity (0,2,0) beats the base .castButton rule, and nothing else in the file sets text-align on castButton.
- The only other centre rule, at line 667, is inside the max-width 900px block, which LiveQA reported already matched at 390px.
- It cannot affect the unsaved button, the open-state fold label (.revealFold) or anything outside the summary.
- No markup, logic or test changes, so no test was expected for a pure CSS alignment rule.
- npm test (318) is green and the build is clean on 50af882.

LiveQA asked for "text-align (and justify)". The span is display inline, the CSS default, so there is no flex justify to match, and text-align alone centres both wrapped lines.

This is a record against this commit's tree, for /sprint-reship's gate. It is not a fresh gate-1 pass and does not replace LiveQA's own retest of the desktop alignment. | commit=50af8820c6f2af6d0c56db2bd06e77378725af1e
